Make Table Meetings supports the date range outside the 1970–2037

ai.s: Stops the Table Meetings list crashing on dates outside 1970–2037 by guarding input and widening how dates are stored.
ai.pr: The date filter sent raw typed dates to the backend, which cast them to a PostgreSQL integer timestamp; any date outside 1970–2037 overflowed and returned HTTP 500.
ai.wy: A scheduling platform cannot have its meetings list fail for dates after 2037.
ai.oc: A frontend guard prevents the crash, and migration to bigint timestamps is recommended to support any realistic date range.

summary: [TechDept] Export finalize must not rely on exact total-count match — add explicit batch tracker

ai.s: Makes queue-based exports finish reliably by tracking batches explicitly instead of waiting for an exact row count that may never be reached.
ai.pr: Exports only completed when the buffer row count exactly equalled the total, so one lost or failed batch left the export stuck in progress forever (the 'stuck at 92.97%' case).
ai.wy: Follow-up to EP-53789, which fixed the immediate cause but not the fragile completion gate.
ai.oc: init records the expected batch count, each batch marks completion idempotently, and finalize runs when all batches are done or failed, for all BaseExport exports.
